correctness.rationale: Scale to R=1 with fixed 0<α<1 and β=1−α. Equality in the disk diameter bound forces antipodes, so compactness localizes the event to the two ordered pairs of tip neighborhoods. In one ordering write inward displacements h,k and heights y,z≥0. The outer circle gives (y−z)²≤y²+z²≤2(h+k)−h²−k², hence 4−D²≥2(h+k−hk). For h,k≤1 this puts each displacement below 2ε and confines both scaled heights to a fixed box. The rescaled exact inner/outer inequalities converge to v²/2≤u≤v²/(2α) and w²/2≤z_scaled≤w²/(2β); the uniform chord expansion then gives deficit s+t+(v+w)²/4 with the two nonnegative excess widths capped by cα v² and cβ w². All constraint boundaries are null, so dominated convergence gives the factor 2ε³/(π²α²β²) times the limiting volume J. Substituting q=v+w, p=v/q and subtracting the two cap-overflow areas and adding their intersection yields J=(4−Iα−Iβ+Iαβ)/12; the radial integral q(1−kq²)_+²/2 is 1/(12k). For the last reciprocal integral the completed-square denominator is c(p−α²/(α²+β²))²+1/[4(α²+β²)] with c=(α²+β²)/(2αβ), confirming both arctangent arguments and the common prefactor. Positive interior gives strict positivity; reflection gives symmetry. In the thin limit 4−Iβ=(8/3)α+O(α²), and |Iαβ−Iα|≤cβ∫₀¹(1/4+cα p²)⁻² dp=O(α^(3/2)), giving the stated coefficient asymptotic only after the fixed-shape limit. The equal-radii arctangent simplification and decimal agree. RESULT.md, VERIFICATION.md and verification_check.py were inspected, not executed. A separate Simpson check of the coefficient integral agreed with the closed form at α=0.2 and 0.5; correctness of the limit rests on the localization and analytic integration, not quadrature.

value.rationale: The two-point distance law is a natural invariant of this classical nonconvex region, and the tail coefficient quantifies the joint effect of its opposite parabolic cusps and area normalization. The exact profile distinguishes shapes with the same cubic power and exposes a singular thin-shape behavior. It directly gives leading expected rare-pair counts in independent samples, without asserting an extreme-value law or uniform two-parameter limit.
